newsitem.title: UK: LME copper sharply lower, bearish, in pre-market.
newsitem.headline: LME copper sharply lower, bearish, in pre-market.

text.p: Copper was down more than $100 early on Wednesday after crumpling under speculative liquidation, and traders said the near term price outlook was even gloomier.
Three months copper traded down to around a key support area at $2,250 per tonne in the pre-market before bouncing weakly to around $2,260. It had closed at $2,368 on Tuesday.
Copper had started to come under pressure during ring trading on Tuesday, and then lost its footing in late inter-office trade as selling intensified.
Falls through $2,350 and $2,325 triggered sell stops and fund selling out of the United States, which encountered more follow-through selling early on Wedensday, traders said.
"When noone responded last night to a bit of buying at $2,320 there was more liquidation through $2,300," a trader said, adding that volumes have been good.
"This morning we've seen banks selling, forcing further liquidation and also delta selling against options."
Further fund selling was possible after Comex opened later in the day, in which case support at $2,220 and then at $2,200 could be tested, traders said.

An LME stock rise of 975 tonnes was unsupportive as recent stock rises and the longer-term perception of more production coming onstream in coming months has been weighing on the market, traders said.
The cash to threes backwardation -- the chief factor supporting the copper price recently -- was $20 narrower amid light lending against options but still quite firm at $115/$120.
"The funds had been running long through the tightness in July/August, but now they're liquidating," a trader said.
"The physical situation isn't that tight and people have been happy to sell forward, which has created resistance that hasn't been overcome. And that's flushed out the funds."
The other base metals were being dragged down in tandem with copper although volumes were generally light.
Aluminum was last trading at $1,555, down $10, after initially testing support around $1,545.
Zinc was also easier at $1,447/1,450, versus $1,460, but traders said it was not threatened by copper-style fund liquidation.
Nickel was down nearly $100 at $6,840 after Tuesday's late burst of strength, on news that workers at Falconbridge's Sudbury facility voted for a strike mandate, petered out.
Tin was little changed at $5,540/5,550 versus $5,540, as was lead at $646/$649 comapred to $649.
Alloy was indicated some $5 lower at $1,420/1,430.
